chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb al-Aqarquqi from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When Ali (peace be upon him) was dismayed by something, he hastened to prayer.
And seek assistance through patience and prayer.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali seek help when faced with distress?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the Prophetic precedent of seeking refuge in prayer during times of overwhelming fear or awe (hawl), emphasizing the psychological and spiritual efficacy of Salat as an immediate divine anchor. This practice underscores the Shia understanding of prayer not merely as ritual obligation but as a transformative mechanism for inner tranquility, directly linking the believer's emotional state to divine assistance through the dual virtues of patience (sabr) and prayer.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al-Fazl Bin ShAzaan , from Hammad Bin Isa, from Shuayb Al-Aqarquqy, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘It was so that whenever something dismayed Aliasws, heasws hastened to the Salāt, then recited this Verse [2:45] And seek Assistance through the patience and the Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Shu’ayb al-‘Aqarqufiy from abu Basir from abu ’Abd Allah, who has said the following: “
If something dismayed Imam Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, he would feel restless for Salah (prayer).
’Seek help from exercising patience and performing Salah (prayer).’”
